label: thm:CFKM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:CFKM}
Let $T:M\to M$ be the map~\eqref{eq:CFKM} with $\alpha\in(1,2]$.
Let $v:M\to{\mathbb R}$ be a H\"older observable with $\int_M v\,d\mu_M=0$ and satisfying $v(0),\,v(1)\neq0$ and $v(0)\neq v(1)$.  It is known (see for example~\cite{CFKM20}) that $a_n^{-1}v_n$ converges in distribution to a two-sided $\alpha$-stable law $X_\alpha$; we denote the density of $X_\alpha$ by $g$.

 Under an aperiodicity assumption that holds typically,
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n\int_M \zeta_1\,\zeta_2\circ T^n\,\xi\circ(v_n-qa_n)\,d\mu_M
=g(q)\int_M \zeta_1\,d\mu_M \int_M \zeta_2\,d\mu_M \int_{\mathbb R} \xi\,d\operatorname{Leb},
\]
for all $\zeta_1,\,\zeta_2\in C_c\big((0,1)\big)$, $\xi\in C_c({\mathbb R})$, $q\in{\mathbb R}$.

label: ex:Thaler
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:Thaler}
We can extend to $C^\eta$ vector-valued observables $v:M\to{\mathbb R}^d$ of Thaler maps (see Section~\ref{sec:LSV}) with $k$ neutral fixed points $x_1,\dots,x_k$ all with exponent $1+1/\alpha$. We again assume that $v(x_i)\neq0$, $i=1,\dots,k$, and we require further that the vectors $\{(v(x_i),1),\, i=1,\dots,k\}$ span ${\mathbb R}^{d+1}$. (In particular, $k\ge d+1$.)
We also assume an aperiodicity assumption that holds typically.
Provided $d<\alpha^2$, we obtain a stable MLLT of the form
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n^d\int_M \zeta_1\,\zeta_2\circ T^n\,\xi\circ(v_n-qa_n)\,d\mu_M
=g(q)\int_M \zeta_1\,d\mu_M \int_M \zeta_2\,d\mu_M \int_{{\mathbb R}^d} \xi\,d\operatorname{Leb},
\]
for all $\zeta_1,\,\zeta_2\in C_c\big(M\setminus\{x_1,\dots,x_k\}\big)$, $\xi\in C_c({\mathbb R}^d)$, $q\in{\mathbb R}^d$.
Here $g$ is the density of the $d$-dimensional $\alpha$-stable law limit for $n^{-1/\alpha}v_n$.

The assumption $d<\alpha^2$ can be 
removed provided $\eta\in(0,1]$ is sufficiently close to $1$ and a further technical condition is satisfied. For this it suffices that $v(x_i)$ has positive first coordinate for all $i=1,\dots,k$.

label: ex:ex
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:ex}
Our results go over almost word for word to nonuniformly expanding semiflows built over intermittent maps of the types in Examples~\ref{ex:CFKM} and~\ref{ex:Thaler}.
See Section~\ref{sec:intflow}. The only differences are that the neutral fixed points become neutral periodic orbits and discrete time $n$ is changed to continuous time $t$.

Also, our results extend almost word for word to uniformly hyperbolic intermittent invertible maps and flows provided that we assume exponential contraction along stable leaves, see Sections~\ref{sec:sol} and~\ref{sec:intflow}.
However, when the contraction along stable leaves is subexponential, our results hold only for a restricted class of H\"older observables.

title: Notation
body_md:
We use ``big O'' and $\ll$ notation interchangeably, writing $a_n=O(b_n)$ or $a_n\ll b_n$
if there are constants $C>0$, $n_0\ge1$ such that
$a_n\le Cb_n$ for all $n\ge n_0$.
We write $a_n\approx b_n$ if $a_n\ll b_n \ll a_n$.
As usual, $a_n=o(b_n)$ means that $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n/b_n=0$
and $a_n\sim b_n$ means that $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n/b_n=1$.

title: Remark
body_md:
(a) Hypothesis \ref{itm:N1} is ``fully nonlattice'': the roof function $\tau$ is ${\mathbb R}$-valued, the observable $w$ is ${\mathbb R}^d$-valued, and \ref{itm:N1} is a nonlattice MLLT for the induced joint observable $\Psi$ which has values in ${\mathbb R}^{d+1}$.
In Section~\ref{sec:YT}, we consider fully lattice and hybrid results for maps where $\tau$ is ${\mathbb Z}$-valued.

\vspace{1ex} \noindent (b)
Hypothesis~\ref{itm:N2} can be relaxed slightly without weakening any of the results. 
Let $\ell_1$ be a slowly varying function.
It suffices that there exists $D>0$ such that \ref{itm:N2} holds as stated for $|z|\le Dn$ and holds with $\tilde\ell$ replaced by $\ell_1$ for $|z|>Dn$. 

\vspace{1ex} \noindent (c)
The dimension restriction in \ref{itm:N3} is somewhat unsatisfactory but the restriction $d\le 2$ is already present in the simpler setting of~\cite{DolgopyatNandori20}, see~\cite[Lemmas~4.3 and~4.6]{DolgopyatNandori20}, and also in~\cite{PeneTerhesiu25}.

\vspace{1ex} \noindent (d)
Assumptions \ref{itm:N1}--\ref{itm:N3} enable us to prove a stable MLLT for the flow modulo a coboundary $H\circ F_t-H$. Dealing with the coboundary is generally considered to be a ``folklore'' result, though the details are often vague  and rely on certain non-explicit topological/metric properties of the underlying probability space (separability, completeness, local compactness). 
Also, it is usually required that $H$ is continuous and bounded, which is not the case in our main examples.

Assumption~\ref{itm:N4} enables us to remain in a purely probabilistic setting in the formulation of Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract}, and the setting is sufficiently flexible for our applications.

 Let $A, B\in{\mathcal A}$.
 Let $K\subset{\mathbb R}^d$ be bounded with $|\partial K|{=0}$ and let $q\in{\mathbb R}^d$. Then writing $x=(y,u)\in Y^\tau$,
\[
  \lim_{t\to\infty}a_t^d\mu^\tau\Big(x\in A\cap F_t^{-1} B:\, W_{N_t(x)}(y)\in qa_t+K\Big)

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The strategy of the proof 
 follows those of~\cite[Lemma 4.3]{AaronsonNakada17},~\cite[Theorem 1]{AaronsonTerhesiu20} and~\cite[Theorem 3.1]{DolgopyatNandori20}.

Write $A=A_0\times I,\,B=B_0\times J\subset {\mathcal A}$
 and set $K_u=K\times(u-J)$.
Let $\omega_t=
  \mu^\tau\big( x \in A\cap F_t^{-1}B:\, W_{N_t(x)}(y)\in qa_t+K\big)$.
For $x=(y,u)\in Y^\tau$, it follows from~\eqref{eq:lap} that
\begin{align*}
\omega_t & = \mu^\tau\big(y\in A_0\cap F^{-N_t(x)}B_0,\,u\in I:\,u+t-\tau_{N_t(x)}(y)\in J,\,W_{N_t(x)}(y)\in qa_t+K\big) \\
  &=\sum_{m\ge0}\mu^\tau\big(y\in A_0\cap F^{-m}B_0,\, u\in I:\, 
\Psi_m(y)  \in (qa_t,t-m{\bar{\tau}})+K_u \big).
 \end{align*}
Let $\gamma\in(\gamma_0,1)$ be as in \ref{itm:N3} for $d\ge \alpha^2$ and $\gamma=0$ otherwise.
By \ref{itm:N3}. 
\[
  \omega_t
 = \sum_{m>t^\gamma}\mu^\tau\big(y\in A_0\cap F^{-m}B_0,\, u\in I:\, 
\Psi_m(y)  \in (qa_t,t-m{\bar{\tau}}) +K_u \big) + o(a_t^{-d})
\]
Hence
\[
  {\bar{\tau}}\omega_t = 
\sum_{m>t^\gamma} \int_I Q_m(t,u)\,du
+ o(a_t^{-d})
\]
where
\[
Q_m(t,u)=\mu\big(y\in A_0\cap F^{-m}B_0:\,
\Psi_m(y)  \in (qa_t,
t-m{\bar{\tau}})+K_u\big).
\]

Fixing $L>0$, we can write
\[
{\bar{\tau}}  \omega_t= S_1(t,L)+S_2(t,L)+o(a_t^{-d})
\]
where
\[
  S_1(t,L)=\sum_{\stackrel{m>t^\gamma:}{|m-t/{\bar{\tau}}|\le La_t}}\int_I Q_m(t,u)\,du, \qquad
  S_2(t,L)=\sum_{\stackrel{m>t^\gamma:}{|m-t/{\bar{\tau}}|> La_t}}\int_I Q_m(t,u)\,du.
\]

Thus, it suffices to show:
\begin{align} \label{eq:S1}
& \lim_{L\to\infty}\lim_{t\to\infty} a_t^d S_1(t,L)=
 {\bar{\tau}} g(q)\mu^\tau(A)\mu^\tau(B)|K|, \\
& \lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_{t\to\infty} a_t^d S_2(t,L)=0.
\label{eq:S2}
\end{align}

In~\eqref{eq:S1}, we are in the range $|m-t/{\bar{\tau}}|\le La_t$.
It follows that
$a_t\sim {\bar{\tau}}^{1/\alpha}a_m$ and $z_{m,t}=\Big(\dfrac{qa_t}{a_m},\dfrac{t-m{\bar{\tau}}}{a_m}\Big)$ is bounded.
By \ref{itm:N1},
\begin{align*}
a_m^{d+1}Q_m(t,u) & =
g_{d+1}(z_{m,t})\mu(A_0)\mu(B_0)|K_u|+h_m(t,u)
\\ &  =
{\bar{\tau}} g_{d+1}(z_{m,t})\mu(A_0)\mu^\tau(B)|K|+h_m(t,u)
\end{align*}
where $\lim_{t\to\infty}h_m(t,u)=0$ uniformly in $|m-t/{\bar{\tau}}|\le La_t$ and $u\in I$.
Hence
\[
a_t^d\int_I Q_m(t,u)\,du  
                                                                                        
={\bar{\tau}}^{2+(d+1)/\alpha} a_t^{-1} g_{d+1}\big(q{\bar{\tau}}^{1/\alpha},(t/{\bar{\tau}}-m){\bar{\tau}}^{1+1/\alpha} a_t^{-1}\big)\kappa+\tilde h_m(t)
\]
where $\kappa=\mu^\tau(A)\mu^\tau(B)|K|$ and
$\tilde h_m(t)=o(a_t^{-1})$ as $t\to\infty$ uniformly in $|m-t/{\bar{\tau}}|\le La_t$.
It follows that
\begin{align*}
  a_t^d  S_1(t,L) 
 ={\bar{\tau}}^{2+(d+1)/\alpha} a_t^{-1}\sum_{|j|\le La_t} 
g_{d+1}\big(q{\bar{\tau}}^{1/\alpha},j{\bar{\tau}}^{1+1/\alpha} a_t^{-1}\big)\kappa+o(1)
\end{align*}
as $t\to\infty$ for each fixed $L$.
Approximating Riemann integrals by Riemann sums with increments of width ${\bar{\tau}}^{1+1/\alpha} a_t^{-1}$ yields
\[
{\bar{\tau}}^{1+1/\alpha} a_t^{-1}
\sum_{|j|\le La_t}
g_{d+1}\big(q{\bar{\tau}}^{1/\alpha},j{\bar{\tau}}^{1+1/\alpha} a_t^{-1}\big)
 \to  
\int_{-L{\bar{\tau}}^{1+1/\alpha}}^{L{\bar{\tau}}^{1+1/\alpha}} g_{d+1}(q{\bar{\tau}}^{1/\alpha},y)\,dy
\]
as $t\to\infty$.
Hence
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty} \lim_{t\to\infty}a_t^dS_1(t,L)
  = {\bar{\tau}}^{1+d/\alpha} g_d(q{\bar{\tau}}^{1/\alpha})\, \kappa
  = {\bar{\tau}} g(q)\, \kappa
\]
by definition of $g_d$ and $g$ in~\eqref{eq:gd}.
This completes the verification of~\eqref{eq:S1}.

\vspace{1ex}
Next, $Q_m(t,u)\le 
\sup_{u\in I} \mu(\Psi_m\in \big(qa_t,t-m{\bar{\tau}})+K_u\big)$.
In~\eqref{eq:S2}, we are
in the range $a_t\ll |m-t/{\bar{\tau}}|$. Hence $|(qa_t,t-m{\bar{\tau}})|\approx |t-m{\bar{\tau}}|$ and it follows from~\ref{itm:N2} that
\[
Q_m(t,u)\ll {\widetilde Q}_m(t) \quad\text{where}\quad
 {\widetilde Q}_m(t)=\frac{m}{a_m^{d+1}}\, \frac{\tilde\ell(|t-m{\bar{\tau}}|)}{|t-m{\bar{\tau}}|^\alpha}\Big(1+\Big(\frac{|t-m{\bar{\tau}}|}{a_m}\Big)^r\Big)
\]
for any $r>0$ sufficiently small.
Hence~\eqref{eq:S2} is an immediate consequence of the next three results.


\begin{prop} \label{prop:1}
\(
\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_{t\to\infty}a_t^d\sum_{La_t<| m-t/{\bar{\tau}}|<ct}{\widetilde Q}_m(t)=0
\)
for all $c\in(0,1/{\bar{\tau}})$.
\end{prop}

\begin{proof}
By the choice of $c$, in this range, $m\approx t$.
Choose $r\in(0,\alpha-1)$. Then
\begin{align*}
\sum_{La_t<  |m-t/{\bar{\tau}}|<ct} {\widetilde Q}_m(t) 
  & \ll \frac{t}{a_t^{d+1}}
\sum_{ m-t/{\bar{\tau}}> L a_t}
\frac{\tilde\ell(m{\bar{\tau}}-t)}{(m{\bar{\tau}}-t)^\alpha} \Big(1+\Big(\frac{m{\bar{\tau}}-t}{a_t}\Big)^r\Big) \\
  & \ll \frac{t}{a_t^{d+1+r}}
\sum_{ m-t/{\bar{\tau}}> L a_t}
\frac{\tilde\ell(m{\bar{\tau}}-t)}{(m{\bar{\tau}}-t)^{\alpha-r}} \\
&  \approx 
\frac{t}{a_t^{d+1+r}} \frac{\tilde\ell(a_t)}{(La_t)^{\alpha-1-r}}
\approx \frac{1}{a_t^d} \frac{1}{L^{\alpha-1-r}}\frac{t\tilde\ell(a_t)}{a_t^{\alpha}}
\end{align*}
by Karamata. 
The result follows since $a_t^\alpha\sim t\tilde\ell(a_t)$.
\end{proof}


\begin{prop} \label{prop:2}
\(
\lim_{t\to\infty}a_t^d\sum_{m-t/{\bar{\tau}} \ge ct}{\widetilde Q}_m(t)=0
\)
for all $c>0$.
\end{prop}

\begin{proof}
In this range, $m\gg t$ so choosing $r\in(0,\alpha-1)$, 
\[
\sum_{ m-t/{\bar{\tau}}\ge ct} {\widetilde Q}_m(t) 
 \ll \frac{t}{a_t^{d+1}}
\sum_{ m-t/{\bar{\tau}}\ge ct}
\frac{\tilde\ell(m{\bar{\tau}}-t)}{(m{\bar{\tau}}-t)^{\alpha-r}}
 \approx \frac{t}{a_t^{d+1}} \frac{\tilde\ell(t)}{t^{\alpha-1-r}}
 =  \frac{1}{a_t^d}\;\frac{\tilde\ell(t)}{t^{\alpha-2-r}a_t}.
\]
By Potter's bounds,
\[
  \frac{\tilde\ell(t)}{t^{\alpha-2-r}a_t}\ll \frac{t^s}{t^{\alpha+1/\alpha-2-r-s}}
=t^{-(\alpha+1/\alpha-2-r-2s)},
\]
for all $s>0$.
Since $\alpha+1/\alpha>2$, we can shrink $r,\,s$ so that $\alpha+1/\alpha>2+r+2s$. Then
  $\dfrac{\tilde\ell(t)}{t^{\alpha-2-r}a_t}=o(1)$
as required.
\end{proof}

\begin{prop} \label{prop:3}
\(
\lim_{t\to\infty}a_t^d\sum_{m\ge t^\gamma,\,m-t/{\bar{\tau}}\le -ct}{\widetilde Q}_m(t)=0
\)
for all $c>0$,
\end{prop}

\begin{proof}
Write the range as $t^\gamma\le m\le c't$ where
$c'=1/{\bar{\tau}}-c$. (If $c'\le0$, then there is nothing to prove.)
Let $r,\,s>0$.
Since $t-m{\bar{\tau}}\gg t$,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{t^\gamma\le m\le c't} {\widetilde Q}_m(t)
\ll \sum_{t^\gamma\le m\le c't}\frac{m}{a_m^{d+1}}\,\frac{\tilde\ell(t)}{t^{\alpha-r}}
& \ll t^{-\alpha+r+s} \sum_{t^\gamma\le m\le c't}\frac{1}{m^{(d+1)/\alpha-s-1}}
\\ & \approx t^{-\alpha+r+s} 
\big\{(t^\gamma)^{2-(d+1)/\alpha+s}
+t^{2-(d+1)/\alpha+s}\big\}.
\end{align*}
Since $\alpha+1/\alpha>2$, we can shrink $r,\,s>0$ so that
\[
a_t^d\sum_{t^\gamma\le m\le c't} {\widetilde Q}_m(t)\ll t^{d/\alpha-\alpha+r+2s}(t^\gamma)^{2-(d+1)/\alpha+s}+o(1).
\]

If $d<\alpha^2$, then $\gamma=0$ and we see immediately that $a_t^d\sum_{1\le m\le c't} {\widetilde Q}_m(t)=o(1)$ for $r,\,s>0$ sufficiently small.

If $d\ge \alpha^2$, then the choice of $\gamma>\gamma_0$ ensures that
$d/\alpha-\alpha+\gamma(2-(d+1)/\alpha)<0$ and the result again follows.
\end{proof}

This completes the proof of the lemma.

label: defn:rv
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defn:rv}
An ${\mathbb R}^m$-valued random variable $X$ is
    \emph{regularly varying} with index $\beta\in{\mathbb R}$ if 
    there exists a Borel probability measure $\sigma$
    on
    ${\mathbb S}^{m-1}$, called the \emph{spectral measure}, such that
\[
        \lim_{t \to \infty}
        \frac{{\mathbb P}(|X| > \lambda t, \ X / |X| \in E)}{{\mathbb P}(|X| > t)}
        = \lambda^{\beta} \sigma(E)
\]
    for all $\lambda > 0$ and all Borel sets $E \subset {\mathbb S}^{m-1}$ with $\sigma(\partial E) = 0$.

label: defn:nondeg
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defn:nondeg}
	A regularly varying random variable $X$ with index $-\alpha$, 
	$\alpha\in(1,2]$, is \emph{nondegenerate} if
\[
\int_{{\mathbb S}^{m-1}}|s\cdot x|^\alpha\,d\sigma(x)>0 
\quad\text{for all $s\in{\mathbb S}^{m-1}$.}
\]

\quad\text{where} \quad N=\sum_{i=1}^k c_i |{\widetilde \omega}_i|^\alpha.
\]

Let $\Psi:Y\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ be an integrable observable with $\int_Y\Psi\,d\mu=0$

$a_n^{-1}\Psi_n\to_d X_\alpha$, where

hypothesis \ref{itm:N2} is satisfied.

Suppose further that $\Psi$ is nondegenerate and aperiodic.

body_md:
\label{prop:N4}
Suppose that $(F,Y,\mu)$ is Gibbs-Markov and that $H:Y^\tau\to{\mathbb R}^d$ has the property that $H|_A:A\to{\mathbb R}^d$ is bounded and uniformly continuous on $A$ for each $A\in{\mathcal A}$. Then $H$ satisfies hypothesis \ref{itm:N4}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $A=A_0\times I\in{\mathcal A}$ and
$\delta>0$.
By uniform continuity of $H|_A$, there exists $N\ge1$ such that $|H(y,u)-H(y',u')|<\delta$
for all $y,y'\in A_0$, $u,u'\in I$ with $s(y,y')>N$ and $|u-u'|<1/N$.

Write $Y$ as a disjoint union of $N$-cylinders $C_1,C_2,\dots$ Since $\sum_{k=1}^\infty \mu(C_k){=1}$, there
exists $r\ge1$ such that
\[
\mu(Y\setminus {\textstyle\bigcup_{k=1}^r }C_k) < {\bar{\tau}} \delta/|I|.
\]
Also, we can partition $I$ into a finite number of intervals $J_1,\dots, J_s$ with $|J_\ell|<1/N$.

Take $\{A_1,\dots,A_n\}=\{(A_0\cap C_k)\times J_\ell:1\le k\le r,\,1\le \ell\le s\}$.
By construction, $A_j\subset A$ and $\operatorname{diam} H(A_j)<\delta$ for each $j$.
Cylinder sets $C_k$ are open and closed, so $\partial C_k=\emptyset$.
Hence $\partial (A_0\cap C_k)\subset\partial A_0$ and it follows that $A_j\in{\mathcal A}$ for each $j$.
Finally,
\begin{align*}
\mu^\tau\Big(A\setminus\bigcup_{j=1}^n A_j\Big)
 & =\mu^\tau\Big(A_0\times I\setminus \bigcup_{k=1}^r (A_0\cap  C_k)\times I\Big)
\\ & =\mu\Big(A_0\setminus \bigcup_{k=1}^r A_0\cap C_k\Big)|I|/{\bar{\tau}}
 \le \mu\Big(Y\setminus \bigcup_{k=1}^r C_k\Big)|I|/{\bar{\tau}}<\delta,
\end{align*}
completing the verification of \ref{itm:N4}.

label: prop:relax
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let
$S_t=\sum_{1\le m\le t^\gamma}\mu^\tau(I_m)$ where
\[
I_m=
\Big\{(y,u)\in Y^\tau:|W_m(y)|\ll a_t,\,
\tau_m(y)\approx t,\,\tau_m(y)\le u+t<\tau_{m+1}(y),\,|u|\ll 1\Big\}.
\]
It suffices to show that $S_t=o(a_t^{-d})$.

Write $W=\omega\tau+Z=\omega\tau-\int_Y\omega\tau\,d\mu+{\widetilde Z}$ where
${\widetilde Z}=Z-\int_Y Z\,d\mu$.
Then ${\widetilde Z}_m=W_m-(\omega\tau)_m+m\int_Y\omega\tau\,d\mu$.
If $|(\omega\tau)_m|\ge c\tau_m$, then  
the conditions $|W_m|\ll a_t$, $\tau_m\approx t$ and $m\ll t^\gamma$ imply that $|{\widetilde Z}_m|\approx t$ since $\gamma<1$. Hence $I_m\subset I_m'\cup I_m''$ where
\begin{align*}
I_m' & =
\Big\{(y,u)\in Y^\tau:|(\omega\tau)_m|< c\tau_m
,\,\tau_m(y)\le u+t<\tau_{m+1}(y),\,|u|\ll 1\Big\},
\\
I_m'' & =
\Big\{(y,u)\in Y^\tau: |{\widetilde Z}_m(y)|\approx t
,\,\tau_m(y)\le u+t<\tau_{m+1}(y),\,|u|\ll 1\Big\}.
\end{align*}

The sets $\{\tau_m(y)\le u+t<\tau_{m+1}(y)\}$ are disjoint, so
\begin{align*}
\sum_{1\le m\le t^\gamma}\mu^\tau(I_m')
& 	\le \mu^\tau\Big(\min_{1\le m\le t^\gamma}|(\omega\tau)_m|/\tau_m < c,\,|u|\ll1\Big)
\\ & \ll
	\mu\Big(\min_{1\le m\le t^\gamma}|(\omega\tau)_m|/\tau_m < c\Big)
=o(a_t^{-d}).
\end{align*}

Similarly,
\[
\sum_{1\le m\le t^\gamma}\mu^\tau(I_m'')
\ll \mu\Big(\max_{1\le m\le t^\gamma}|{\widetilde Z}_m|\gg t\Big).
\]
It follows from~\eqref{eq:Psireg} that ${\widetilde Z}$ is piecewise H\"older.
Since  ${\widetilde Z}\in L^2$,
standard moment estimates~\cite{M09b} for Gibbs-Markov maps yield
$\big|\max_{1\le m\le t}|{\widetilde Z}_m|\,\big|_p\ll t^{1/2}$.
By the definitions
\[
p(1-\tfrac12 \gamma_0)=\tfrac12 p\, \frac{d+\alpha^2-4\alpha+2}{d+1-2\alpha}>\frac{d}{\alpha}.
\]
Hence we can shrink $\gamma>\gamma_0$ so that by Markov's inequality,
\[
\sum_{1\le m\le t^\gamma}\mu^\tau(I_m'')
\ll (t^\gamma)^{p/2}/t^p = t^{-p(1-\frac12\gamma)}=o(a_t^{-d}),
\]
completing the proof.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $p_0\in Y$ be a fixed point for $F$ and let $p_n\in Y$, $n\ge1$, be a sequence of periodic points $F^np_n=p_n$.
The sequence of periodic points has \emph{good asymptotics} for $\Psi:Y\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ if 
\begin{itemize}
\item
\(
\Psi_n(p_n)=n\Psi(p_0)+\kappa+J_n\gamma^n+o(\gamma^n)\)
as $n\to\infty$,
where $\gamma\in(0,1)$, $\kappa,\,J_n\in{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$.
\item For any $b\in {\mathbb S}^d$, it holds that
$b\cdot J_{n}=E_{n}\cos(n\theta+\theta_{n})$ where $E_{n}$ is a bounded sequence of real numbers with $\liminf_{n\to\infty}|E_{n}|>0$, and either (i) $\theta=\theta_{n}=0$ for all $n$, or
(ii) $\theta\in(0,\pi)$ and $\theta_{n}\in(\tilde\theta-\pi/12,\tilde\theta+\pi/12)$ for some $\tilde\theta$.
\end{itemize}
head: environment

label: prop:good
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:good} Assume that $\Psi:Y\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:Psireg}.
Let $p_n$, $n\ge1$, be a sequence of periodic points with good asymptotics for $\Psi$. Then $\Psi$ is aperiodic.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that there exist $\phi:Y\to{\mathbb S}^1$ measurable, $\lambda\in{\mathbb S}^1$ and $s\in{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ such that $\phi\circ F=\lambda e^{is\cdot\Psi}\phi$.
A Liv\v{s}ic regularity result for Gibbs-Markov maps~\cite[Theorem~1.1]{Gouezel06} (see also~\cite{BruinHollandNicol05}) guarantees that $\phi$ has a version that is continuous on partition elements.
By the definition of aperiodicity, Definition~\ref{defn:aperiodic},
we are required to show that $s=0$.

Note that $\phi\circ F^n=\lambda^n e^{is\cdot\Psi_n}\phi$.
In particular, we can evaluate $\phi$ at  $p_n=F^np_n$ to obtain
$\lambda^n e^{is\cdot\Psi_n(p_n)}=1$. 
Similarly, 
$\lambda e^{is\cdot\Psi(p_0)}=1$, and so 
$e^{is\cdot\{\Psi_n(p_n)-n\Psi(p_0)\}}=1$.
By good asymptotics,
\[
s\cdot (\kappa+J_n\gamma^n+o(\gamma^n))\equiv 0 \bmod 2\pi.
\]
Letting $n\to\infty$ yields $s\cdot\kappa=0\bmod 2\pi$ and 
hence
\[
s\cdot (J_n\gamma^n+o(\gamma^n))\equiv 0 \bmod 2\pi.
\]
For $n$ sufficiently large, we obtain 
$s\cdot (J_n\gamma^n+o(\gamma^n))\equiv 0$ and hence
$s\cdot J_n\to0$.
If $s\neq0$, then write
$s\cdot J_n=E_n\cos(n\theta+\theta_n)$ as in the definition of good asymptotics.
In case (i), we have $s\cdot J_n=E_n\to0$ contradicting the $\liminf$ condition on $E_n$. In case (ii), there is a subsequence $n_k$ with $\cos(n_k\theta+\theta_{n_k})$ bounded away from zero leading to the same contradiction.
Hence $s=0$ completing the proof.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The two-sided Gibbs-Markov maps that we have in mind are essentially the base of a two-sided Young tower as in~\cite{Young98} (except that we do not require full-branches for ${\bar F}$). We have followed~\cite[Section~7.1]{BMT21} in omitting much of the structure often associated with Young towers, mentioning only those properties required in the sequel.
In particular, we have not mentioned a product structure, 
and
we have not made explicit the quotienting procedure (along local stable leaves) that passes from $F$ to ${\bar F}$.

Of course, our class of two-sided Gibbs-Markov maps trivially includes the one-sided Gibbs-Markov maps considered in Section~\ref{sec:GM}. However,  the definition is flexible enough to include genuinely two-sided maps.

label: lem:GM2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:GM2}
Let $(F_t,Y^\tau,\mu^\tau)$ be a Gibbs-Markov flow.
Given $w:Y^\tau\to{\mathbb R}^d$ integrable with $\int_{Y^\tau}w\,d\mu^\tau=0$,
define
$\Psi=(W,{\tilde \tau}):Y\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ and $H:Y^\tau\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ as in Section~\ref{sec:abstract}.
Assume that $\Psi:Y\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ is regularly varying with index $-\alpha$,  $\alpha\in(1,2]$. Suppose also
that $\Psi$ admits a decomposition of the form
\begin{equation} \label{eq:chi}
\Psi={\bar{\Psi}}\circ\bar\pi+\chi\circ F-\chi,
\end{equation}
where ${\bar{\Psi}}:{\bar Y}\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:Psireg} and
$\chi\in L^\infty(Y,{\mathbb R}^{d+1})$. Then
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)]
$a_n^{-1}\Psi_n\to_d X_\alpha$, where
$X_\alpha$ is as in~\eqref{eq:X} and~\eqref{eq:X2}.
\item[(b)]
Suppose further that $\Psi$ is nondegenerate. Then hypothesis~\ref{itm:N2} is satisfied.
\item[(c)]
Suppose moreover that $\Psi$ is nondegenerate and aperiodic, and that
$\chi|_A:A\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ is uniformly continuous
for each $A\in{\mathcal A}$.
Then hypothesis \ref{itm:N1} is satisfied with
$g_{d+1}$ being the density for the random vector $X_\alpha$
in part~(a).
\end{itemize}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\chi$ is in $L^\infty$ and $\bar\pi$ is a measure-preserving semiconjugacy, it is immediate that ${\bar{\Psi}}$ is regularly varying function on $({\bar Y},{\bar{\mu}})$ with the same index $-\alpha$  and spectral measure $\sigma$ as $\Psi$.
Moreover, ${\bar{\Psi}}$ is nondegenerate (resp.\ aperiodic) if and only if $\Psi$ is.

Since ${\bar{\Psi}}$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:Psireg}, 
Lemma~\ref{lem:GM}(a,b) applies to ${\bar{\Psi}}:{\bar Y}\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ and hence to ${\bar{\Psi}}\circ\bar\pi:Y\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$. Since $\Psi_n={\bar{\Psi}}_n\circ \bar\pi+\chi\circ F^n-\chi$,
it follows that parts~(a) and~(b) are satisfied for $\Psi:Y\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$.

Part~(c) follows by Theorem~\ref{thm:LLTtwo}.

title: Remark
body_md:
As in Section~\ref{sec:GM}, aperiodicity is typical and is a $C^2$ open $C^r$ dense condition. To see this, 
suppose that $\phi\circ F=\lambda e^{is\cdot \Psi}\phi$ with $\phi$ measurable.
Then $\tilde\phi\circ F=\lambda e^{is\cdot{\bar{\Psi}}\circ{\bar{\pi}}}\tilde\phi$
where $\tilde\phi=\phi\,e^{-is\cdot\chi}$.
Again, $\tilde\phi$ has a continuous version, and therefore so does $\phi$. Hence the existence of periodic orbits with good asymptotics for $\Psi$ rules out aperiodicity by the same argument as in Section~\ref{sec:GM}.
Provided $\Psi$ is $C^r$, $r\ge2$, on two partition elements of $Y$, good asymptotics holds for a $C^2$ and $C^r$ dense set of $\Psi$.

label: thm:abstract-lattice
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:abstract-lattice}
Assume \ref{itm:L1}--\ref{itm:L4}.
 Let $A, B\in{\mathcal A}$ and let $q\in{\mathbb R}^d$. Then 
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}a_n^d\mu_\Delta\Big(x\in A\cap f_\Delta^{-n}B:\, w_n(x)-[n{\bar w}]= [qa_n]\Big)
  = g(q)\mu_\Delta(A)\mu_\Delta(B).
 \]
head: environment
name: Stable MLLT for $w$

title: Proof
body_md:
This is similar to the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract}, so we only sketch the details. (Generally, the arguments are simpler, except that we have to take care of centring.)

Write $x=(y,j)\in \Delta$. Then
$f_\Delta^nx=(F^{N_n}y,j+n-R_{N_n}(y))$ where
$N_n=N_n(x)$ is such that
$R_{N_n}(y)\le j+n<R_{N_n+1}(y)$.
Note that
\[
w_n(x)=W_{N_n(x)}(y)+H(f_\Delta^nx)-H(x).
\]

By the argument in Subsection~\ref{sec:pf2}, it suffices to prove
the following analogue of Lemma~\ref{lem:abstract}.
Let $A=A_0\times\{i\},\,
B=B_0\times\{j\}\in{\mathcal A}$ and let $q\in{\mathbb R}^d$. 
We must show that
\begin{equation} \label{eq:absYT}
\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n^d \mu_\Delta\Big(x\in A\cap f_\Delta^{-n}B: W_{N_n(x)}(y)=[qa_n]+[n{\bar w}]\Big)=g(q)\mu_\Delta(A)\mu_\Delta(B).
\end{equation}

Define
\[
Q_m(n)=\mu \Big(y\in A_0\cap F^{-m}B_0:
{\widehat \Psi}^{(m)}(y)=([qa_n]+[n{\bar w}]-[m{\bar w}{\bar{R}}],n-[m{\bar{R}}]+k)\Big),
\]
where $k=i-j$.
Arguing as before, for $L>0$,
\[
{\bar{R}} \mu_\Delta\Big(x\in A\cap f_\Delta^{-n}B: W_{N_n(x)}(y)=[qa_n]+[n{\bar w}]\Big)=S_1(n,L)+S_2(n,L)+o(a_n^{-d})
\]
where
\[
S_1(n,L)= \sum_{\stackrel{m>n^\gamma}{|m-n/{\bar{R}}|\le La_n}}Q_m(n), \qquad
S_2(n,L)= \sum_{\stackrel{m>n^\gamma}{|m-n/{\bar{R}}|> La_n}}Q_m(n).
\]
Here, $\gamma\in(\gamma_0,1)$ is as in \ref{itm:L3} for $d\ge\alpha^2$ and $\gamma=0$ otherwise.

For the range of $m$ in $S_1$, we use \ref{itm:L1} to show uniform convergence
\[
a_m^{d+1}Q_m(n)=
g_{d+1}(z_{m,n})\mu(A_0)\mu(B_0)+o(1) ={\bar{R}}^2
g_{d+1}(z_{m,n})\mu_\Delta(A)\mu_\Delta(B)+o(1) ,
\]
where $z_{m,n}=\Big(\dfrac{qa_n+n{\bar w}-m{\bar w}{\bar{R}}}{a_m},\dfrac{n-m{\bar{R}}}{a_m}\Big)$.
Continuing as in the proof of~\eqref{eq:S1}, we obtain that
	\begin{align*}
		& a_n^d  S_1(n,L)
		\\ &\; ={\bar{R}}^{2+(d+1)/\alpha} a_n^{-1}
\sum_{|j|\le La_n}
		g_{d+1}\big(q{\bar{R}}^{1/\alpha}+{\bar w} j{\bar{R}}^{1+1/\alpha}a_n^{-1},j{\bar{R}}^{1+1/\alpha} a_n^{-1}\big)\mu_\Delta(A)\mu_\Delta(B)+o(1). 
\end{align*}
	Approximating Riemann integrals by Riemann sums with increments of width ${\bar{R}}^{1+1/\alpha} a_n^{-1}$ yields
\begin{align*}
	{\bar{R}}^{1+1/\alpha} a_n^{-1}\sum_{|j|\le La_n}
	g_{d+1}\big(q{\bar{R}}^{1/\alpha}+{\bar w} & j{\bar{R}}^{1+1/\alpha} a_n^{-1},j{\bar{R}}^{1+1/\alpha} a_n^{-1}\big)
 \\ & \to  
	\int_{-L{\bar{R}}^{1+1/\alpha}}^{L{\bar{R}}^{1+1/\alpha}} g_{d+1}(q{\bar{R}}^{1/\alpha}+{\bar w} y,y)\,dy
\end{align*}
as $n\to\infty$.
Hence
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n^d S_1(n,L)=
 {\bar{R}}^{1+d/\alpha} g_d(q{\bar{R}}^{1/\alpha})\mu_\Delta(A)\mu_\Delta(B)=
 {\bar{R}} g(q)\mu_\Delta(A)\mu_\Delta(B).
\]

For the range of $m$ in $S_2$, we have 
\[
|([qa_n]+[n{\bar w}]-[m{\bar w}{\bar{R}}],n-[m{\bar{R}}]+k)|\approx |n-m{\bar{R}}|.
\]
Proceeding as in the proof of~\eqref{eq:S2}, we obtain
that
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty} a_n^d S_2(n,L)=0.
\]
This completes the proof of~\eqref{eq:absYT}.

\label{rmk:g}
In \ref{itm:N1}, $g_{d+1}$ is the limiting density corresponding to the observable
$\Psi=(W,{\tilde \tau})$ which is centred.
Hence, $g_d$ as defined in~\eqref{eq:gd} is the limiting density corresponding to the induced observable $W=\sum_{j=0}^{\tau-1}w\circ f_\Delta^j$.

The definition of $g_d$ in~\eqref{eq:gdL} takes into account the fact that $w$ and $W$ are no longer centred. Indeed, define the induced centred observable 
$Z=\sum_{j=0}^{R-1}(w-{\bar w})\circ f_\Delta^j$.
In \ref{itm:L1}, $g_{d+1}$ is the limiting density corresponding to the observable
$\Psi-{\bar{\Psi}}$ where $\Psi=(W,R)=(Z+{\bar w} R,R)$,
In particular, $g_d$ is the limiting density corresponding to $Z$.

Hence we see that in both \ref{itm:N1} and \ref{itm:L1}, $g_d$ is the limiting density corresponding to the induced centred observable.

 Define $Z=W-\omega R\in L^p$ and ${\widetilde Z}=Z-\int_Y Z\,d\mu$.
 Then proceeding as before yields ${\widetilde Z}_m=n{\bar w}-(\omega R)_m+o(n)$ and we have to deal with the extra term $n{\bar w}$. $|(\omega R)_m|\le cR_m$ for all $m$. 
 Then \ref{itm:L3} holds provided $Z=W-\omega R\in L^p$ for some 
$p$ sufficiently large as before.

label: rmk:aperiodic
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk:aperiodic}
A sufficient condition for aperiodicity can be formulated as follows.
Suppose that $\phi:Y\to{\mathbb S}^1$ is measurable and satisfies $\phi\circ F=\lambda e^{is\cdot\Psi}\phi$ for some $s\in{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ and $\lambda\in{\mathbb S}^1$.
By Liv\v{s}ic regularity~\cite[Theorem~1.1]{Gouezel06}, $\phi$ has a continuous version.
Let $y_1,y_2,\ldots\in \bigcup_{b\in\beta}b$ be fixed points for $F$.
Then $(\Psi(y_i)-\Psi(y_j))\cdot s\equiv0\bmod 2\pi$ for all $i,j$.
Form a $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ matrix $A\in {\mathbb Z}^{(d+1)\times (d+1)}$ with each row given by a vector of the form $\Psi(y_i)-\Psi(y_j)$ for some $i,j$. Then $As\equiv0\bmod (2\pi{\mathbb Z})^{d+1}$. If $\det A=\pm1$, then inverting yields that $s\equiv0\bmod (2\pi{\mathbb Z})^{d+1}$ and hence $\Psi$ is aperiodic.

label: lem:NUEflow
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) Define
\[
V:X\to{\mathbb R}^d, \qquad  V=\int_0^r v\circ T_u\,du.
\]
For $x,x'\in X$ with $r(x')\le r(x)$,
\begin{align*}
|V(x)-V(x')| & \le \int_0^{r(x)}|v(T_ux)-v(T_ux')|\,du \;+\;|v|_\infty |r(x)-r(x')|
\\
& \le |v|_\eta\int_0^{|r|_\infty}d(T_ux,T_ux')^\eta\,du \;+\;|v|_\infty |r|_\eta\,d(x,x')^\eta
\\
& \le C^\eta |v|_\eta |r|_\infty\,d(x,x')^\eta \;+\;|v|_\infty |r|_\eta\,d(x,x')^\eta
\ll d(x,x')^\eta.
\end{align*}
Hence $V$ is $C^\eta$.

Next, notice that
$W=\int_0^\tau v\circ T_u\,du=\sum_{j=0}^{R-1}V\circ T^j$. Hence for $y,y'\in b$, $b\in\beta$, 
\[
|W(y)-W(y')|\le |V|_\eta \sum_{j=0}^{R(y)-1}d(T^jy,T^jy')^\eta
\ll (R|_b) d_{\theta_1}(y,y').
\]
where $\theta_1=\theta^\eta$.
Replacing $V$ by $r$ yields
\[
|{\tilde \tau}(y)-{\tilde \tau}(y')|= |\tau(y)-\tau(y')|\ll (R|_b) d_{\theta_1}(y,y'),
\]
so $|\Psi(y)-\Psi(y')|\ll(R|_b) d_{\theta_1}(y,y')$.
But $\tau\ge(\inf r)R$ so $R|_b\ll (\inf r)^{-1} {\textstyle{\inf_b}}\tau$.
Hence
\[
|\Psi(y)-\Psi(y')|\ll 
({\textstyle{\inf_b}}\tau) d_{\theta_1}(y,y')
=({\textstyle{\inf_b}}{\tilde \tau}+{\bar{\tau}}) d_{\theta_1}(y,y')
\ll ({\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|+1) d_{\theta_1}(y,y'),
\]
verifying~\eqref{eq:Psireg}.

\vspace{1ex} \noindent (b) 
Note that $H(y,u)=\int_0^uv(T_ty)\,dt$.
Set $K=\sup I$.
Then $|H(y,u)|\le K|v|_\infty$ so $H|_A$ is bounded.

For $(y,u),\,(y',u)\in A$,
\begin{align*}
|H(y,u)-H(y',u)|
& \le K\sup_{t\in[0,K]}|v(T_ty)-v(T_ty')|
\\ & \le K|v|_\eta \sup_{t\in[0,K]}d(T_ty,T_ty')^\eta
\ll d(y,y')^\eta.
\end{align*}
Also, $|H(y,u)-H(y,u')|\le |v|_\infty\, |u-u'|$.
 Hence $H|_A$ is uniformly continuous.

label: thm:NUEflow
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:NUEflow}
Let $(T_t,M,\mu_M)$ be a nonuniformly expanding semiflow.
Let $v:M\to{\mathbb R}^d$ be a bounded H\"older observable with $\int_M v\,d\mu_M=0$.

Suppose that
$\Psi$ is aperiodic, nondegenerate, regularly varying with index $-\alpha$,  $\alpha\in(1,2]$ and spectral measure $\sigma$. Let $g_{d+1}$ be the density for the corresponding stable law $X_\alpha$ in~\eqref{eq:X} and~\eqref{eq:X2} and
define $g$ as in~\eqref{eq:gd}.
 Assume that $d<\alpha^2$.

Let ${\mathcal A}$ be the collection of measurable subsets $A\subset Y$ 
where
$\mu(\partial A)=0$.

Then $v$ satisfies a stable MLLT: setting $v_t=\int_0^t v\circ T_s\,ds$,
\[
  \lim_{t\to\infty}a_t^d\mu_M\Big(x\in A\cap T_t^{-1} B:\, v_t(x)\in qa_t+K\Big)
  = g(q)\mu_M(A)\mu_M(B)|K|
 \]
 for all $A, B\in{\mathcal A}$, all
 $K\subset{\mathbb R}^d$ bounded with $|\partial K|=0$ and all $q\in{\mathbb R}^d$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\pi:Y^\tau\to M$ is a measure-preserving semiconjugacy, it suffices to prove the MLLT for $w=v\circ\pi:Y^\tau\to{\mathbb R}^d$.

By Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract}, we reduce to verifying hypotheses \ref{itm:N1}--\ref{itm:N4}
for $\Psi:Y\to{\mathbb R}^{d+1}$ and $H:Y^\tau\to{\mathbb R}^d$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:NUEflow}(a), $\Psi$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:Psireg}, so \ref{itm:N1} and \ref{itm:N2} follow from Lemma~\ref{lem:GM}.
Hypothesis~\ref{itm:N4} follows from
Lemma~\ref{lem:NUEflow}(b) and Proposition~\ref{prop:N4}.
Hypothesis~\ref{itm:N3} is vacuously satisfied since $d<\alpha^2$.

label: rmk:N3
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk:N3}
The assumption that $d<\alpha^2$ can be relaxed as in Section~\ref{sec:relax}.

label: rmk:NUEmap
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk:NUEmap}
The same result and proof holds (with the obvious modifications) for nonuniformly expanding maps $(T,M,\mu_M)$ and mean zero bounded H\"older observables $v:M\to{\mathbb R}^d$.
The conclusion is that
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}a_n^d\mu_M\Big(x\in A\cap T^{-n}B:\, v_n(x)\in qa_n +K\Big)
  = g(q)\mu_M(A)\mu_M(B)|K|. 
\]

Similarly, the result holds for 
nonuniformly expanding maps $(T,M,\mu_M)$ and H\"older observables $v:M\to{\mathbb Z}^d$,
 but H\"older means that $v$ is bounded and constant on $T^jb$ for all $b\in\beta$ and $0\le j<R|_b$.
The conclusion is that
\[
  \lim_{n\to\infty}a_n^d\mu_M\Big(x\in A\cap T^{-n}B:\, v_n(x)-[n{\bar v}]= [qa_n]\Big)
  = g(q)\mu_M(A)\mu_M(B).
 \]

label: prop:LSV
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:LSV}
Define $\omega:Y\to{\mathbb R}$, $\omega|_{Y_i}=v(i)$, $i=0,1$.
Then $W=\omega R+Z$ where $Z\in L^p$ for some $p>\alpha$.
Moreover, $Z\in L^\infty$ provided that $\eta\in(1/\alpha,1]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Shrinking $\eta$ if necessary, we can suppose that $\eta\neq 1/\alpha$.
We recall the standard calculation (see for example~\cite{Gouezel04}).
For $y\in Y_0$,  
\[
|Z(y)|=|W(y)-v(0)R(y)|
=\Big|\sum_{j=0}^{R(y)-1}(v(T^j y)-v(0))\Big|
\le |v|_\eta \sum_{j=0}^{R(y)-1}(T^j y)^\eta.
\]
We have $T^jy\approx (R(y)-j)^{-\alpha}$, so
\[
|Z(y)|\ll \sum_{j=1}^{R(y)}j^{-\eta\alpha}\ll 
  1+ R(y)^{1-\eta\alpha}. 
\]
Similarly for $y\in Y_1$, and the result follows.
head: environment

title: Theorem \refthm:CFKM
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:LSV}, we can apply Proposition~\ref{prop:jointrv}
to deduce that $\Psi=(W,R)$ is regularly varying and nondegenerate. 
By assumption, $d=1<\alpha^2$ and $\Psi$ is aperiodic.
Hence we have verified the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:NUEflow}
(more precisely, Remark~\ref{rmk:NUEmap}).
In this way, we obtain a stable MLLT relative to intervals $A$, 
$B\subset Y$.

For intermittent maps, it is well-known how to enlarge $Y$ to contain $[{\epsilon},1-{\epsilon}]$ for ${\epsilon}>0$ arbitrarily small. Hence we can take 
$A$ and $B$ to be arbitrary intervals in $M$ that are bounded away from $0$ and $1$. The result is now a consequence of Lemma~\ref{lem:vague}.~
head: environment

label: prop:LSV1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:LSV1}
Define $\omega:Y\to{\mathbb R}$, $\omega|_{Y_i}=\omega_i$, $i=0,1$.
Then $W=\omega\tau+Z$ where $Z\in L^p$ for some $p>\alpha$.
Moreover, $Z\in L^\infty$ provided that $\eta\in(1/\alpha,1]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that
\[
W(y)=\int_0^{\tau(y)} v(y,u)\,du=
\sum_{j=0}^{R(y)-1}\int_0^{r(T^jy)}v(T_u T^jy)\,du.
\]
In particular,
\[
W(x_i)=
\sum_{j=0}^{R(x_i)-1}\int_0^{r(x_i)}v(T_ux_i)\,du
=R(x_i)r(x_i)\omega_i = \omega_i\tau(y).
\]
Therefore for $y\in Y_i$,  
\[
Z(y)
=W(y)-W(x_i)=\sum_{j=0}^{R(y)-1}\Big\{\int_0^{r(T^j y)}v(T_uT^j y)\,du-
\int_0^{r(x_i)}v(T_ux_i)\,du\Big\}.
\]
Now $\int_0^{r(T^j y)}v(T_uT^j y)\,du- \int_0^{r(x_i)}v(T_ux_i)\,du=I_1+I_2$ where
\[
I_1  =\int_0^{r(T^j y)}\big\{v(T_uT^j y)-
v(T_ux_i)\big\}\,du, \qquad
 I_2  = \int_{r(x_i)}^{r(T^j y)}v(T_uT^j y)\,du.
\]

Our assumptions on $v$, $r$ and $T_t$ ensure that
\[
|I_1|,\,|I_2| \ll |T^j y-x_i|^\eta
\approx |R(y)-j|^{-\alpha\eta}.
\]
Hence
\[
|Z(y)| 
\ll
\sum_{j=1}^{R(y)}j^{-\alpha\eta}
\approx R(y)^{1-\alpha\eta}+1.
\]
(We suppose without loss that $\eta\neq 1/\alpha$.)
The result follows.
head: environment

label: cor:LSVflow
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:LSVflow}
Let $T_t:M\to M$ be the intermittent semiflow above with parameter $\alpha\in(1,2]$. Suppose that $v:M\to{\mathbb R}$ is $C^\eta$ and that
$\omega_i$ are nonzero and not all equal.
Assume that $\Psi=(W,{\tilde \tau}):Y\to{\mathbb R}^2$ is aperiodic.
Then the stable MLLT holds:
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}a_t\int_M \zeta_1\,\zeta_2\circ T_t\,\xi\circ(v_t-qa_t)\,d\mu_M
=g(q)\int_M \zeta_1\,d\mu_M \int_M \zeta_2\,d\mu_M \int_{{\mathbb R}^d} \xi\,d\operatorname{Leb},
\]
for all $\zeta_1,\,\zeta_2\in C_c\big(M\setminus\{p_0,p_1\}\big)$ and $\xi\in C_c({\mathbb R})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:LSV1}, we can apply Proposition~\ref{prop:jointrv} to deduce that $\Psi$ is regularly varying and nondegenerate.
By assumption, $d=1<\alpha^2$ and $\Psi$ is aperiodic.
Hence we have verified the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:NUEflow} 
and the result follows.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Intermittent semiflows with several neutral periodic orbits and ${\mathbb R}^d$-valued observables work the same way, subject to the restrictions concerning $d$.
Our results also cover invertible intermittent flows, but we require either exponential contraction along stable leaves or restrictions on the observable.

label: lem:vague
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:vague}
Suppose that
\begin{equation} \label{eq:vague}
\lim_{t\to\infty}a_\gamma(t) {\mathbb P} (\omega\in A\cap F_t^{-1}B:\,
\zeta_{t,\gamma}(\omega)\in E) = {\mathbb P}(A){\mathbb P}(B)\operatorname{Leb}(E)
\end{equation}
uniformly in $\gamma\in\Gamma$,
for all $A,B\in{\mathcal A}$, $E\in{\mathcal E}$.
Suppose that $H_1,H_2:\Omega\to{\mathbb R}^m$ satisfy property~\ref{itm:H}.
Then
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}a_\gamma(t) {\mathbb P} \left(\omega\in A\cap F_t^{-1}B:\, \zeta_{t,\gamma}(\omega)+H_1(\omega)+H_2(F_t\omega)\in E\right) = {\mathbb P}(A){\mathbb P}(B)\operatorname{Leb}(E)
\]
uniformly in $\gamma\in\Gamma$,
for all $A,B\in{\mathcal A}$, $E\in{\mathcal E}$.
head: environment

label: eq:port
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $A,\,B\in{\mathcal A}$ and 
introduce the family of measures
${\mathbb Q}_t(D)=a_\gamma(t)\, {\mathbb P}(A\cap F_t^{-1}B\cap D)$ on ${\mathbb R}^m$.
Also, let ${\mathbb Q}(D)={\mathbb P}(A){\mathbb P}(B)\operatorname{Leb}(D)$.
Define
\[
S^{t,\gamma}:\Omega\to{\mathbb R}^m, \qquad
S^{t,\gamma}=\zeta_{t,\gamma}+H_1+H_2\circ F_t.
\]
We are required to prove that
$\lim_{t\to\infty}S^{t,\gamma}_*\,{\mathbb Q}_t(E)={\mathbb Q}(E)$ for all
$E\in{\mathcal E}$.
Note that $S^{t,\gamma}_*\,{\mathbb Q}_t({\mathbb R}^m)=a_\gamma(t)$, so the measures $S^{t,\gamma}_*\,{\mathbb Q}_t$ are trivially Radon measures (finite on compact sets).
Also ${\mathbb Q}$ is a Radon measure.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:Port} below,
 it suffices to prove that
\begin{equation} \label{eq:port}
\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}g\,d S^{t,\gamma}_*\,{\mathbb Q}_t=\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}g\,d{\mathbb Q}
\end{equation}
uniformly in $\gamma$, for all $g\in C_c({\mathbb R}^m)$.

Let $g\in C_c({\mathbb R}^m)$, and define
\[
G:({\mathbb R}^m)^3\to {\mathbb R},
\qquad G(x,y,z)=g(x+y+z).
\]
We claim that
\begin{align} \label{eq:vagueclaim} \nonumber
\lim_{t\to +\infty}a_\gamma(t)&\int_{A\cap F_t^{-1}B}G(H_1(\omega),H_2(F_t \omega),\zeta_{t,\gamma}(\omega))\, d{\mathbb P}(\omega)\\
&=\int_{A\times B\times{\mathbb R}^m}G(H_1(\omega),H_2(\omega'),z)d({\mathbb P}\times{\mathbb P}\times\operatorname{Leb})(\omega,\omega',z)  
\end{align}
uniformly in $\gamma$.
Suppose that the claim is true. Then by definition of $G$,
\begin{align*}
\lim_{t\to +\infty}a_\gamma(t)&\int_{A\cap F_t^{-1}B}g(\zeta_{t,\gamma}(\omega)+H_1(\omega)+H_2(F_t \omega))\, d{\mathbb P}(\omega)\\
&=\int_{A\times B\times{\mathbb R}^m}g(H_1(\omega)+H_2(\omega')+z)d({\mathbb P}\times{\mathbb P}\times\operatorname{Leb})(\omega,\omega',z) 
\\ &=\int_{A\times B\times{\mathbb R}^m}g(z)d({\mathbb P}\times{\mathbb P}\times\operatorname{Leb})(\omega,\omega',z) 
\end{align*}
uniformly in $\gamma$,
yielding~\eqref{eq:port}.

It remains to prove the claim.
	Since $g$ is compactly supported and $H_1(A)$, $H_2(B)$ are bounded, we can find a closed disk $D\subset{\mathbb R}^m$ 
	such that $\operatorname{supp} G\subset {\mathbb R}^m\times{\mathbb R}^m\times D$.
For any ${\epsilon}>0$,
there exists $\delta\in(0,{\epsilon}/\{\operatorname{Leb}(D)(\| G\|_\infty+1)\})$ such that 
\begin{equation} \label{eq:G}
|G(x,y,z)-G(x',y',z')|<{\epsilon} \quad\text{for all}\quad
|x-x'|<\delta,\ |y-y'|<\delta,\ |z-z'|<\delta.
\end{equation} 
We partition $D$ into a finite number of disjoint compact
subsets $C_1,C_2,\dots$ with $\operatorname{Leb}(\partial C_k)=0$ and $\operatorname{diam} C_k<\delta$.

Since $H_1$, $H_2$ satisfy \ref{itm:H}, we can choose
disjoint subsets $A_i\subset A$ and disjoint subsets 
$B_j\subset B$ with $A_1,\dots,A_m;\,B_1,\dots,B_n\in{\mathcal A}$ such that
\begin{alignat}{2} \label{eq:N4a}
& {\mathbb P}(A\setminus A') < \delta, & \qquad 
& {\mathbb P}(B\setminus B') < \delta, \\
\label{eq:N4b}
& \max_{1\le i\le m} \operatorname{diam} H_1(A_i)  < \delta , & \qquad
& \max_{1\le j\le n} \operatorname{diam} H_2(B_j)  < \delta ,
\end{alignat}
where $A'=\bigcup_{i=1}^mA_i$ and $B'=\bigcup_{j=1}^nB_j$.

Now,
\begin{align*}
a_\gamma(t) & \int_{A\cap F_t^{-1}B}  G(H_1(\omega),H_2(F_t \omega),\zeta_{t,\gamma}(\omega))\, d{\mathbb P}(\omega)
\\ & =
a_\gamma(t)\int_{A\cap F_t^{-1}B\cap\zeta_{t,\gamma}^{-1}D}  G(H_1(\omega),H_2(F_t \omega),\zeta_{t,\gamma}(\omega))\, d{\mathbb P}(\omega)
\\ & =
a_\gamma(t)\int_{A'\cap F_t^{-1}B'\cap\zeta_{t,\gamma}^{-1}D}G(H_1(\omega),H_2(F_t \omega),\zeta_{t,\gamma}(\omega))\, d{\mathbb P}(\omega)+I_1(t)+I_2(t),
\end{align*}
where
\begin{align*}
|I_1(t,\gamma)| & \le \|G\|_\infty\, a_\gamma(t)\,
{\mathbb P}\big((A\setminus A')\cap F_t^{-1}B\cap \zeta_{t,\gamma}^{-1}D\big), \\
|I_2(t,\gamma)| & \le \|G\|_\infty\, a_\gamma(t)\,
{\mathbb P}\big(A'\cap F_t^{-1}(B\setminus B')\cap \zeta_{t,\gamma}^{-1}D\big).
\end{align*}
By~\eqref{eq:vague} and~\eqref{eq:N4a},
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}a_\gamma(t)\,
{\mathbb P}\big((A\setminus A')\cap F_t^{-1}B\cap \zeta_{t,\gamma}^{-1}D\big)
={\mathbb P}(A\setminus A'){\mathbb P}(B)\operatorname{Leb}(D)<\delta\operatorname{Leb}(D)
\]
uniformly in $\gamma$.
Hence $\limsup_{t\to\infty}\sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma}|I_1(t,\gamma)|<\delta\|G\|_\infty\operatorname{Leb}(D)<{\epsilon}$.
Similarly, $\limsup_{t\to\infty}\sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma}|I_2(t,\gamma)|<{\epsilon}$.

Next, by~\eqref{eq:G} and~\eqref{eq:N4b},
\begin{align*}
a_\gamma(t) & \int_{A'\cap F_t^{-1}B'\cap\zeta^{-1}D} G(H_1(\omega),H_2(F_t \omega),\zeta_{t,\gamma}(\omega))\, d{\mathbb P}(\omega) \\
&= \sum_{i,j,k} a_\gamma(t) \int_{A_i\cap F_t^{-1}B_j\cap \zeta_{t,\gamma}^{-1}C_k}G(H_1(\omega),H_2(F_t \omega),\zeta_{t,\gamma}(\omega))\, d{\mathbb P}(\omega) \\
&= \sum_{i,j,k}  \Big\{\min_{H_1(A_i)\times H_2(B_j)\times C_k}G\Big\} a_\gamma(t){\mathbb P}(A_i\cap F_t^{-1}B_j\cap \zeta_{t,\gamma}^{-1}C_k)+I_3(t,\gamma),
\end{align*}
where
\[
|I_3(t,\gamma)|\le \delta\sum_{i,j,k} a_\gamma(t){\mathbb P}(A_i\cap F_t^{-1}B_j\cap \zeta_{t,\gamma}^{-1}C_k).
\]
Hence $\limsup_{t\to\infty}|I_3(t,\gamma)|\le \delta{\mathbb P}(A){\mathbb P}(B)\operatorname{Leb}(D)<{\epsilon}$.

By~\eqref{eq:vague},
\begin{align*}
 \lim_{t\to\infty} \sum_{i,j,k} &   \Big\{\min_{H_1(A_i)\times H_2(B_j)\times C_k}G\Big\} a_\gamma(t){\mathbb P}(A_i\cap F_t^{-1}B_j\cap \zeta_{t,\gamma}^{-1}C_k)
\\ & \qquad =
 \sum_{i,j,k}    \Big\{\min_{H_1(A_i)\times H_2(B_j)\times C_k}G\Big\} {\mathbb P}(A_i){\mathbb P}(B_j)\operatorname{Leb}(C_k).
\end{align*}
Reversing the first two steps of the calculations in a simpler situation,
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{i,j,k}    & \Big\{\min_{H_1(A_i)\times H_2(B_j)\times C_k}G\Big\} {\mathbb P}(A_i){\mathbb P}(B_j)\operatorname{Leb}(C_k).
\\ & =
\int_{A\times B\times {\mathbb R}^m}G(H_1(\omega),H_2(\omega'),z)\,d({\mathbb P}\times{\mathbb P}\times\operatorname{Leb})(\omega,\omega',z)+I_4,
\end{align*}
where $|I_4|\le \delta\operatorname{Leb}(D)+2\delta\|G\|_\infty\operatorname{Leb}(D)<3{\epsilon}$.

Since ${\epsilon}>0$ is arbitrary, the claim~\eqref{eq:vagueclaim} follows.

title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, suppose that (a) holds and let $K\subset {\mathbb R}^m$ be compact.
Choose a sequence of compact sets $K_j\subset{\mathbb R}^m$ and a sequence
of functions
$f_j\in C_c({\mathbb R}^m)$ such that
$K_{j+1}\subset K_j$, $\bigcap_j K_j=K$, and
$1_K\le f_j\le 1_{K_j}$ for all $j$.
Then by (a), for each fixed $j$,
\[
\lambda_t^\gamma(K)\le \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}f_j\,d\lambda_t^\gamma\to \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}f_j\,d\lambda
\]
uniformly in $\gamma$.
Hence $\limsup_{t\to\infty} \sup_\gamma \lambda_t^\gamma(K)\le \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}f_j\,d\lambda$.
Also, $|f_j|\le 1_{K_1}$ which is $\lambda$-integrable and $f_j\to 1_K$ pointwise as $j\to\infty$, so by the dominated convergence theorem $\limsup_{t\to\infty} \sup_\gamma \lambda_t^\gamma(K)\le \lambda(K)$.


Second, continue to suppose that (a) holds and let $G\subset{\mathbb R}^m$ be open and bounded. 
Choose a sequence of open sets $G_j\subset{\mathbb R}^m$ and a sequence of functions
$f'_j\in C_c({\mathbb R}^m)$ such that
$G_j\subset G_{j+1}$, $\bigcup_j G_j=G$, and
$1_G\ge f'_j\ge 1_{G_j}$. Then the same argument as before (but with dominating function $1_G$) shows that
$\liminf_{t\to\infty} \inf_\gamma \lambda_t^\gamma(G)\ge \lambda(G)$.

Now let $E\in{\mathcal E}_\lambda$. Taking $K=\bar E$ and noting that $E\subset K$ and $\lambda(K)=\lambda(E)$, it follows from the first calculation that
$\limsup_{t\to\infty} \sup_\gamma \lambda_t^\gamma(E)\le \lambda(E)$.
Similarly, taking $G=\operatorname{Int} E$ it follows from the second calculation that
$\liminf_{t\to\infty} \inf_\gamma \lambda_t^\gamma(E)\ge \lambda(E)$.
This completes the proof that (a) implies (b).

Next, we show that (b) implies (a). Let $g\in C_c({\mathbb R}^m)$, and set $M=\sup|g|$. 
There exists $R>0$ such that $\operatorname{supp} g\subset B_R(0)$.
Note that $\lambda(\partial B_r(0))>0$ for at most countably many $r\in [R, R+1]$. Hence there exists $r>0$ such that $D=\overline{B_r(0)}$ contains $\operatorname{supp} g$ and $D\in{\mathcal E}_\lambda$.

Given ${\epsilon}>0$, choose $c_0<c_1<\dots<c_k$ such that $[-M,M]\subset(c_0,c_k)$ and $c_i-c_{i-1}<{\epsilon}$ for $i=1,\dots,k$.
Since $\lambda(g=c)>0$ for at most countably many values of $c$, we can arrange that $\lambda(g=c_i)=0$ for $i=1,\dots,k$.

Let $E_i=g^{-1}(c_{i-1},c_i)$. Then $\partial E_i\subset \{g=c_{i-1}\}\cup\{g=c_i\}$ so $\lambda(\partial E_i)=0$.
Hence $E_i\cap D\in{\mathcal E}_\lambda$.
(Note that one of the $E_i$ contains ${\mathbb R}^m\setminus\operatorname{supp} g$ which is unbounded, hence the need to intersect with the bounded set $D$.)
By (b), there exists $T>0$ such that
\begin{equation} \label{eq:D1}
\Big|\sum_{i=1}^k c_i\lambda_t^\gamma(E_i\cap D)-
\sum_{i=1}^k c_i\lambda(E_i\cap D)\Big|\le {\epsilon} ,
\end{equation}
for all $t>T$, $\gamma$.

By definition of $E_i$, 
\[
c_{i-1}\lambda_t^\gamma(E_i\cap D)\le 
\int_{E_i\cap D}g\,d\lambda_t^\gamma
\le c_i\lambda_t^\gamma(E_i\cap D),
\]
for all $t$, $\gamma$, $i$. Since $\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}g\,d\lambda_t^\gamma=\int_Dg\,d\lambda_t^\gamma$, it follows that
\begin{equation} \label{eq:D2}
\Big|\int_{{\mathbb R}^m} g\,d\lambda_t^\gamma-\sum_{i=1}^k c_i\lambda_t^\gamma(E_i\cap D)\Big|<{\epsilon} \lambda_t^\gamma( D),
\end{equation}
for all $t$, $\gamma$.
Similarly,
\begin{equation} \label{eq:D3}
\Big|\int_{{\mathbb R}^m} g\,d\lambda-\sum_{i=1}^k c_i\lambda(E_i\cap D)\Big|<{\epsilon} \lambda(D).
\end{equation}
Since $D\in{\mathcal E}_\lambda$, by (b) we can increase $T$ if need be so that $\lambda_t^{\gamma}(D)\le \lambda(D)+1$
for all $t>T$, $\gamma$.
This together with~\eqref{eq:D1},~\eqref{eq:D2},~\eqref{eq:D3}, yields that
\[
\sup_\gamma\Big|\int_{{\mathbb R}^m} g\,d\lambda_t^\gamma-\int_{{\mathbb R}^m} g\,d\lambda\Big|
<2{\epsilon}(1+\lambda(D)),
\]
for all $t>T$.
Since ${\epsilon}>0$ is arbitrary, this completes the proof that (b) implies (a).

We have the revised estimate $\|\partial_qQ(s+h)-\partial_qQ(s)\|
\ll |h|^{\alpha-1}\tilde\ell(1/|h|)(1+(|s|/|h|)^r)$ leading to
\begin{equation} \label{eq:Q}
\|\partial_q(Q(s+h)^n)-\partial_q(Q(s)^n)\|\ll 
\delta_1^n|h|^{\alpha-1}\tilde\ell(1/|h|)(1+(|s|/|h|)^r).
\end{equation}

The proof now proceeds as in~\cite[p.~13]{MT22} until the estimates of the expressions $F_1,\dots,F_6$.
As an example,
\[
F_2 =\frac{n}{|x|}\int_{\Pi_{2{\epsilon}}}|\lambda(s_2)|^{n-1} |\partial_q\lambda(s_1)-\partial_q\lambda(s_2)|\|P(s_2)\|\,ds
\]
where $|x|\ge \pi/{\epsilon}$, 
$\{s_1,s_2\}=\{s,s-h\}$ and $h\approx 1/|x|$.
Applying the estimates in~\cite{MT22} with the modification from condition~(2)(iv), 
\begin{align*}
F_2 & \ll \frac{n}{|x|}\int_{\Pi_{2{\epsilon}}} e^{-c(n-1)|s_2|^\alpha\tilde\ell(1/|s_2|)}|x|^{-(\alpha-1)}\tilde\ell(|x|)(1+|s_2x|^r)\,ds 
\\ & \le \frac{n}{|x|}\int_{\Pi_{3{\epsilon}}} e^{-c(n-1)|s|^\alpha\tilde\ell(1/|s|)}|x|^{-(\alpha-1)}\tilde\ell(|x|)(1+|sx|^r)\,ds
\\ & = n\frac{\tilde\ell(|x|)}{|x|^\alpha}\int_{\Pi_{3{\epsilon}}} e^{-c(n-1)|s|^\alpha\tilde\ell(1/|s|)}\,ds
+ n\frac{\tilde\ell(|x|)}{|x|^{\alpha-r}}\int_{\Pi_{3{\epsilon}}} s^r e^{-c(n-1)|s|^{\alpha}\tilde\ell(1/|s|)}\,ds.
\end{align*}
By~\cite[Lemma~2.3]{MT22}, 
$\int_{\Pi_{3{\epsilon}}} s^\beta e^{-c(n-1)|s|^{\alpha}\tilde\ell(1/|s|)}\,ds
\ll a_n^{-(m+\beta)}$ for $\beta\ge0$, so
\[
F_2\ll \frac{n}{a_n^m}\frac{\tilde\ell(|x|)}{|x|^\alpha}
\Big(1+\Big(\frac{|x|}{a_n}\Big)^r\Big).
\]
This estimate is the same as in~\cite{MT22} except for the extra
factor of $1+\big(\frac{|x|}{a_n}\big)^r$.
Similarly, the estimates in~\cite{MT22} for $F_1$ and $F_5$ are unchanged except for this same factor, while the estimates for $F_3$ and $F_4$ are completely unchanged. Finally, using~\eqref{eq:Q},
$F_6\ll \delta_1^n 
\frac{\tilde\ell(|x|)}{|x|^{\alpha-r}}
\ll \frac{n}{a_n^{m+r}}
\frac{\tilde\ell(|x|)}{|x|^{\alpha-r}}$.~

label: thm:LLD
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:LLD}
Let $(F,Y,\mu)$ be a mixing Gibbs-Markov map with associated partition $\beta$ and $\theta\in(0,1)$.
Fix $r\in(0,\alpha-1)$ and $\theta_0\in(0,1)$. 
Suppose that there is a constant $C_0$ such that
\begin{equation} \label{eq:Psireg0}
|\Psi(y)-\Psi(y')|\le C_0({\textstyle{\inf_b}} |\Psi|+1)d_{\theta_0}(y,y')
\quad\text{for all $y,y'\in b$, $b\in\beta$}.
\end{equation}
Then for all $h>0$, there is a constant $C$ such that
\[
\mu\{\Psi_n\in\Pi_h(x)\}\le C\frac{n}{a_n^m}\frac{\tilde\ell(|x|)}{1+|x|^\alpha}\Big(1+\Big(\frac{|x|}{a_n}\Big)^r\Big)
\quad\text{for all $n\ge1$, $x\in{\mathbb R}^m$}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Without loss, we can suppose that $h\in(0,1)$.
Increase $\theta$ if necessary so that $\theta\in(\theta_0^r,1)$.
Given $v:Y\to{\mathbb R}^d$,  we let
\[
D_{b,\theta}\,v=\sup_{y,y'\in b,\,y\neq y'}|v(y)-v(y')|/d_\theta(y,y'),
\qquad |v|_\theta=\sup_{b\in\beta}D_{b,\theta}v.
\]
We take ${\mathcal B}={\mathcal F}_\theta$ to be the Banach space of functions $v:Y\to{\mathbb R}$ such that $|v|_\theta<\infty$ with norm $\|v\|_\theta=|v|_\infty+|v|_\theta$.
It remains to verify conditions (1) and~(2) in Lemma~\ref{lem:absLLD}.

Since $R(0)$ does not depend on $\Psi$, condition~(1) is unchanged from~\cite{MT22}. We focus here on conditions (2)(ii) and (2)(iv); the other parts of condition~(2) are simpler.

As in the proof of~\cite[Proposition~3.10]{MT22}, we note that
\[
\|R(v\chi)\|_\theta \ll \|v\|_\theta\sum_{b\in\beta} \mu(b)({\textstyle{\sup_b}}|\chi|+D_{b,\theta}\chi)
\]
for $\chi:Y\to{\mathbb C}$.
Hence
$\|\partial_q R(s)\|\ll \sum_{b\in\beta} \mu(b)({\textstyle{\sup_b}}|\chi|+D_{b,\theta}\chi)$ with 
$\chi=\Psi_q e^{is\cdot \Psi}$.
Now ${\textstyle{\sup_b}}|\chi|={\textstyle{\sup_b}}|\Psi|_q\ll {\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|+1$
and $D_{b,\theta}\psi\le D_{b,\theta_0}\psi\ll{\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|+1$. 
For $y,y'\in b$,
we have
\begin{align*}
|e^{is\cdot \Psi(y)}-e^{is\cdot \Psi(y')}| & \le \min\{|s||\Psi(y)-\Psi(y')|,2\}
 \le 2|s|^r|\Psi(y)-\Psi(y')|^r
\\ & \ll |s|^r ({\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|^r+1) d_{\theta_0}(y,y')^r
\le |s|^r({\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|^r+1) d_\theta(y,y'),
\end{align*}
so $D_{b,\theta}e^{is\cdot \Psi}\ll |s|^r({\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|^r+1)$.
It follows that
\[
\|\partial_q R(s)\|\ll \sum_{b\in\beta} \mu(b)({\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|+{\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|^{1+r}+1)\le |\Psi|_1+|\Psi|_{1+r}^{1+r}+1<\infty
\]
by the choice $r<\alpha-1$.
This completes the proof of (2)(ii).

Turning to (2)(iv), 
$\|\partial_qR(s+h)-\partial_qR(s)\|\ll \sum_{b\in\beta} \mu(b)({\textstyle{\sup_b}}|\chi|+D_{b,\theta}\chi)$ with
$\chi=\Psi_q e^{is\cdot \Psi}(e^{ih\cdot \Psi}-1)$. 
As in~\cite{MT22}, there are four terms to estimate, the most difficult of which is
\[
S=\sum_{b\in\beta} 
 {\textstyle{\sup_b}} |\Psi_q|\, {\textstyle{\sup_b}} |e^{ih\cdot \Psi}-1|\,D_{b,\theta}e^{is\cdot \Psi}.
\]
We have already seen that
${\textstyle{\sup_b}} |\Psi_q| \ll {\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|+1$ and $D_{b,\theta}e^{is\cdot \Psi}\ll
|s|^r ({\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|^r+1)$.
Also, ${\textstyle{\sup_b}} |e^{ih\cdot \Psi}-1|\le 
\min\{h{\textstyle{\sup_b}}|\Psi|,2\}\ll
\min\{h({\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|+1),1\}$.
Hence
\begin{align*}
S& \ll 
|s|^r \sum_{b\in\beta} \mu(b)({\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|^{1+r}+1) \min\{h({\textstyle{\inf_b}}|\Psi|+1),1\}
\\ & \le |s|^r \int_Y (|\Psi|^{1+r}+1) \min\{h(|\Psi|+1),1\}\,d\mu.
\end{align*}

Let $G(x)=\mu(|\Psi|\le x)$ denote the distribution function of $|\Psi|$, so
$1-G(x)=x^{-\alpha}\ell(x)$ for $x>0$.
Then for $K>1$,
\[
S\ll  |s|^r \int_0^\infty (x^{1+r}+1) \min\{h(x+1),1\}\,dG(x)
\ll  |s|^r(hI_1+I_2)
\]
where
$I_1=\int_0^K (x^{2+r}+1) \,dG(x)$ and
$I_2=\int_K^\infty x^{1+r}\,dG(x)$.
Since $r\in(0,\alpha-1)$, we can proceed as in the proof of~\cite[Lemma~2.2(ii)]{MT22} to obtain
$I_1\ll K^{2-\alpha+r}\ell(K)$ and 
$I_2\ll K^{1-\alpha+r}\ell(K)$.
Taking $K\approx 1/h$, we obtain the estimate
$S \ll |s|^r\ell(1/h)h^{\alpha-1-r}$.
The other three terms in (2)(iv) are more easily estimated using the ideas seen already and are bounded by
$\tilde\ell(1/h)h^{\alpha-1}$.
Hence we obtain the desired estimate in (2)(iv).

title: Proof
body_md:
Properties (a)--(d) are unchanged from Subsection~\ref{app:N2}.
Since $a_n^\alpha\sim n\tilde\ell(a_n)$, it follows from~(d) that
$|\lambda(a_n^{-1}s)|^n\le \exp\{-nc|a_n^{-1}b|^\alpha \tilde\ell(a_n/|s|)\}
\le \exp\{-\frac12 c |s|^\alpha \tilde\ell(a_n/|s|)\tilde\ell(a_n)^{-1}\}$
for $n$ large. By Potter's bounds, there exists $c'$ such that
$|\lambda(a_n^{-1}s)|^n\le \exp\{-c'|s|^{\alpha'}\}$ for $n$ large,
proving~(e).

To prove part (f), 
first define the characteristic function
$\phi(s)=\int_Y e^{is\cdot\Psi}\,d\mu$, $s\in{\mathbb R}^m$.
Since $\Psi$ is in the domain of the stable law $X_\alpha$, we have that
$\lim_{n\to\infty}\phi(a_n^{-1}s)^n= {\mathbb E}(e^{is\cdot X_\alpha})$.

Following the proof of~\cite[Lemma~3.5]{MT22}, for $|s|<{\epsilon}$,
\[
\lambda(s)=\phi(s)+H(s)
\quad\text{where} \quad H(s)=O(|s|^2).
\]
Hence
\(
\lambda(s)= \phi(s)(1+{\widetilde H}(s))
\)
where ${\widetilde H}(s)=H(s)\phi(s)^{-1}$.
Shrinking ${\epsilon}$ so that $|\phi(s)|{>\frac12}$ for $|s|<{\epsilon}$,
we have ${\widetilde H}(s)=O(|s|)^2$. 

Now fix $s\in{\mathbb R}^m$ and consider $n$ large so that $a_n^{-1}|s|<{\epsilon}$. Then 
\[
n{\widetilde H}(a_n^{-1}s)\ll na_n^{-2}\sim n^{1-2/\alpha}\tilde\ell(a_n)^{-2/\alpha}
=o(1),
\]
 so $\lim_{n\to\infty}n{\widetilde H}(a_n^{-1}s)=0$.
Hence,
\[
\lambda(a_n^{-1}s)^n=
\phi(a_n^{-1}s)^n(1+{\widetilde H}(a_n^{-1}s))^n
\sim \phi(a_n^{-1}s)^n \exp\{n{\widetilde H}(a_n^{-1}s)\}
\to {\mathbb E}(e^{is\cdot X_\alpha})
\]
as $n\to\infty$, completing the proof of~(f).

label: prop:ap
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It is standard that the 
spectral radius of $R(s)$ is at most $1$ and
the essential spectral radius of $R(s)$ is less than $1$ for all $s$.
We claim that there are no eigenvalues on the unit circle for $s\neq0$.
Then the spectral radius is less than $1$ for all $s\neq0$ and the result follows from
continuity of $s\mapsto R(s)$.

It remains to prove the claim. Suppose that there exist
$\lambda\in {\mathbb S}^1$ and $v\in{\mathcal F}_\theta$ such that
$R(s)v=\lambda v$.
Define $U_s:L^2\to L^2$, $U_sv=e^{-is\cdot {\widetilde \Psi}}v\circ F$.
Then $U_s$ is the $L^2$ adjoint of $R(s)$ and a calculation shows that
$\|U_sv-\bar\lambda v\|_2=0$.
Hence $v\circ F=\bar\lambda e^{is\cdot {\widetilde \Psi}}v$.
In particular, $|v|\circ F=|v|$, so $|v|\equiv1$ by ergodicity.
Since $s\neq0$, this violates the aperiodicity assumption. We conclude that there are no eigenvalues on the unit circle, verifying the claim.

label: lem:LLT
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:LLT}
Let $g\in C_c({\mathbb R}^m)$ and define
\begin{align*}
G_{n,z} & =
 \int_{{\mathbb R}^m} g(s)\int_Y \zeta_1(s)\;\zeta_2(s)\circ F^n e^{is\cdot {\widetilde \Psi}_n}\,d\mu\,ds, \\ 
 I_{n,z} & =
 \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}1_{\{|s|< {\epsilon} }\} g(s)
\Big(\int_Y \zeta_1(s)\,d\mu\Big)
\Big(\int_Y \zeta_2(s)\,d\mu\Big)
\lambda(s)^n  \,ds.
\end{align*}

There is a constant $C>0$ such that
\[
|G_{n,z}- I_{n,z}|
\le C\big({\textstyle\sup_s}\|\zeta_1(s)\|\,|\zeta_2(s)|_1\big)
a_n^{-(m+1)}, 
\]
for all $\zeta_1:{\mathbb R}^m\to {\mathcal F}_\theta$, $\zeta_2:{\mathbb R}^m\to  L^1$, $n\ge1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that
\[
G_{n,z}
 =\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}g(s)\int_Y \zeta_2(s)\, R(s)^n\zeta_1(s) \,d\mu\,ds.
\]

Let ${\epsilon}>0$ be as in Proposition~\ref{prop:R} and
choose $M>{\epsilon}$ so that $\operatorname{supp} g\subset B_M(0)$.
By Proposition~\ref{prop:R}(a), for $|s|\le{\epsilon}$,
\[
R(s)^n=\lambda(s)^nP(0)+\lambda(s)^n(P(s)-P(0))+Q(s)^n.
\]
Hence
\(
G_{n,z}= I_1+I_2+I_3+I_4
\)
where
\begin{align*}
I_1 & = \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}
1_{\{|s|<{\epsilon}\}} g(s)\int_Y\zeta_2(s) \lambda(s)^n P(0) \zeta_1(s)\,d\mu\,ds
\\ & = \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}
1_{\{|s|<{\epsilon}\}} g(s)\mu(\zeta_1(s))\mu(\zeta_2(s))\lambda(s)^n \,ds, 
\\
I_2 & = \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}
1_{\{|s|<{\epsilon}\}}g(s)
\int_Y \zeta_2(s)\, \lambda(s)^n \big(P(s)-P(0)\big) \zeta_1(s)
\,d\mu\,ds, \\
I_3 & = \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}
1_{\{|s|<{\epsilon}\}}g(s)
\int_Y \zeta_2(s)\, Q(s)^n \zeta_1(s)
\,d\mu\,ds, \\
I_4 & = \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}
1_{\{{\epsilon}\le |s|\le M\}}g(s)
\int_Y \zeta_2(s)\, R(s)^n \zeta_1(s) \,d\mu\,ds.
\end{align*}

By Proposition~\ref{prop:ap},
\begin{align*}
|I_4|  
& \le |g|_\infty\, \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}
1_{\{{\epsilon}\le |s| \le M\}}
|\zeta_2(s)|_1\, |R(s)^n\zeta_1(s)|_\infty \,ds \\ & 
\le |g|_\infty\, \int_{{\mathbb R}^m}
1_{\{{\epsilon}\le |s| \le M\}}
|\zeta_2(s)|_1\, \|R(s)^n\| \|\zeta_1(s)\|\,ds
\ll \kappa\delta_0^n,
\end{align*}
where $\kappa= {\textstyle \sup_s}\|\zeta_1(s)\| \,|\zeta_2(s)|_1$.
Similarly, by Proposition~\ref{prop:R}(c), $|I_3|\ll   
 \kappa \delta_0^n$.
Also,
\begin{align*}
|I_2| & \ll  
 \kappa 
\int_{{\mathbb R}^m} 1_{\{|s|< {\epsilon}\}}
   |\lambda(s)|^n\|P(s)-P(0)\|\,ds
\ll  \kappa\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}\exp\{-nc|s|^\alpha \tilde\ell(1/|s|)\} |s|\,ds
\end{align*}
by Proposition~\ref{prop:R}(b,d). A change of variables (\cite[Lemma~2.3]{MT22})
now shows that $|I_2|\ll \kappa a_n^{-(m+1)}$.

title: Theorem \refthm:LLT
body_md:
Define the family of measures on ${\mathbb R}^{m_1}$,
\[
\nu_{n,z}(K)=a_n^m\,\int_Y \zeta_1\;\zeta_2\circ F^n\;1_{\{u_n\in z_1a_n+K\}}
1_{\{{\hat v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\,d\mu.
\]
Also define $\nu_z(K)=g_{X_\alpha}(z)
\int_Y\zeta_1\,d\mu\, \int_Y\zeta_2\,d\mu\, |K|$.
We claim that $\lim_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z}\int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}}h\,d\nu_{n,w}=\int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}} h\,d\nu_z$
for all $h\in L^1({\mathbb R}^{m_1})$ with compactly supported Fourier transform $\hat h$.
It then follows from~\cite[Theorem~10.7]{Breiman} that 
$\lim_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z}\nu_{n,w}(K)\to\nu_z(K)$ for all $K\subset{\mathbb R}^{m_1}$ bounded with $|\partial K|=0$. 
Now fix such a $K$. It follows easily that 
$\lim_{n\to\infty}\nu_{n,w}(K)\to\nu_w(K)$ uniformly for $w$ in a neighbourhood of $z$ 
for each fixed $z\in{\mathbb R}^m$. By compactness, we obtain uniform convergence for $|z|\le L$.

It remains to verify the claim.
Note that
$h(x)=\int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}}e^{is_1\cdot x}\hat h(s_1)\,ds_1$ and
\begin{align*}
1_{\{{\hat v}^{(n)}=[w_2a_n]\}}
& =(2\pi)^{-m_2}\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^{m_2}}e^{-is_2\cdot [w_2a_n]}e^{is_2\cdot {\hat v}^{(n)}}\,ds
\\ & =
(2\pi)^{-m_2}\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^{m_2}}e^{-is_2\cdot([w_2a_n]+c_n)}e^{is_2\cdot {\tilde v}_n}\,ds,
\end{align*}
where ${\tilde v}=v-\int_Y v\,d\mu$ and
$c_n=\big[n\int_Y v\,d\mu\big]-n\int_Y v\,d\mu$.
By Fubini,
\begin{align*}
& \int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}}h\,d\nu_{n,w}
 =a_n^m\int_Y \zeta_1\;\zeta_2\circ F^n\, h(u_n-w_1a_n)1_{\{{\hat v}^{(n)}=[w_2a_n]\}}\,d\mu
\\ & \quad =(2\pi)^{-m_2}a_n^m\int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}\times[-\pi,\pi]^{m_2}}e^{-i s_1\cdot w_1a_n}e^{-is_2\cdot([w_2a_n]+c_n)}\hat h(s_1)\int_Y \zeta_1\;\zeta_2\circ F^n\, e^{is\cdot {\widetilde \Psi}_n}\,d\mu\,ds.
\end{align*}
Let $\zeta=(2\pi)^{-m_2}\mu(\zeta_1)\mu(\zeta_2)$.
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:LLT}
with 
\[
g(s)=e^{-i s_1\cdot w_1a_n}e^{-is_2\cdot([w_2a_n]+c_n)}\hat h(s_1)1_{\{s_2\in[-\pi,\pi]^{m_2}\}},
\]
we obtain
\begin{align*}
\int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}}h\,d\nu_{n,w}
& =a_n^m \zeta
 \int_{|s|< {\epsilon} }e^{-is_1\cdot w_1a_n}e^{-is_2\cdot([w_2a_n]+c_n)} \hat h(s_1)\lambda(s)^n\, ds +O(a_n^{-1})
\\ & = 
\zeta
\int_{|s|< a_n {\epsilon} }e^{-is_1\cdot w_1}e^{-ia_n^{-1}s_2\cdot([w_2a_n]+c_n)} \hat h(a_n^{-1}s_1) \lambda(a_n^{-1}s)^nds + O(a_n^{-1}).
\end{align*}
By Proposition~\ref{prop:R}(e,f),
it follows from the dominated convergence theorem that
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z}  
\int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}}h\,d\nu_{n,w} = 
\zeta
\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}\hat h(0)\,e^{-is\cdot z}\, {\mathbb E}(e^{is\cdot X_\alpha})\,ds.
\]
Tracking through the definitions,
\[
\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}\hat h(0)\,e^{-is\cdot z}\, {\mathbb E}(e^{is\cdot X_\alpha})\,ds=
\hat h(0)(2\pi)^m g_{X_\alpha}(z)
=(2\pi)^{m_2}\int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}}h(x)\,dx\,g_{X_\alpha}(z).
\]
Hence, we have shown that
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z} \int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}}h\,d\nu_{n,w}=
g_{X_\alpha}(z)
\mu(\zeta_1)\mu(\zeta_2)
\int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}} h\,dx =\int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}}h\,d\nu_z,
\]
as required.

Let $\beta_n$ be the set of closures of $n$-cylinders in $Y$
and let $\beta=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\beta_n$.
Using the greedy algorithm, we write $\operatorname{Int} A$ as a disjoint countable union $\operatorname{Int} A=\bigcup_{j\ge 1}b_j$ where $b_j\in \beta$.
(At the $j$'th step, choose $b_j\in\beta$ such that $\mu(b_j)\ge\frac12\sup\{b\in \beta:b\subset \operatorname{Int} A\setminus (b_1\cup\dots\cup b_{j-1})$.)
Setting $A_1=\bigcup_{j=1}^J b_j$ we obtain $A_1\subset A$ such that $1_{A_1}\in{\mathcal F}_\theta$ and $\mu(A)-\mu(A_1)<{\epsilon}/2$.
Similarly, we construct $D\subset \operatorname{Int} A^c$ such that $1_D\in{\mathcal F}_\theta$ and $\mu(A^c)-\mu(D)<{\epsilon}/2$.
Let $A_2=D^c$. Then $1_{A_2}=1_Y- 1_D\in{\mathcal F}_\theta$
and $\mu(A_2)-\mu(A)<{\epsilon}/2$.~

label: cor:LLT

title: Proof
body_md:
The result is immediate from Theorem~\ref{thm:LLT} if we suppose in addition that
$1_A\in{\mathcal F}_\theta$, so it remains to relax this condition.
For this step, we can regard $B$ and $K$ as fixed.
Let $A\subset Y$ be measurable with $\mu(\partial A)=0$ and let ${\epsilon}>0$.
Choose $A_1,A_2$ as in Proposition~\ref{prop:A}.
Let 
\[
q_{n,z}(E)=a_n^m\,\mu(y\in E\cap F^{-n}B:u_n(y)\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\hat v}^{(n)}(y)=z_2a_n)
\]
and set $c=g_{X_\alpha}(z)\mu(B)|K|$.
Then
\begin{align*}
c\mu(A_1) & =\lim_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z} q_{n,w}(A_1)
\le \liminf_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z} q_{n,w}(A)
\\ &\le \limsup_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z} q_{n,w}(A)
 \le \lim_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z} q_{n,w}(A_2)=c\mu(A_2).
\end{align*}
Hence
$c(\mu(A)-{\epsilon})\le \liminf_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z} q_{n,w}(A)
\le \limsup_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z} q_{n,w}(A)
\le c(\mu(A)+{\epsilon})$.
Since ${\epsilon}>0$ is arbitrary,
$\lim_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z}q_{n,w}(A)=c\mu(A)$ and the result follows.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\gamma\in(0,1)$.
Recall that a test function $\zeta:Y\to{\mathbb R}$ is dynamically H\"older if $\zeta$ is bounded and there exist constants $C>0$, $\gamma\in(0,1)$ such that $|\zeta(F^ny)-\zeta(F^ny')|\le C(\gamma^{s(y,y')}+\gamma^{s(y,y')-n})$ for all
$y,y'\in Y$ and $n\ge0$.

First, we prove the MLLT with $1_A$ and $1_B$ replaced by dynamically H\"older test functions
$\zeta_1,\zeta_2:Y\to{\mathbb R}$.
Define
\[
\zeta_{r,k}:Y\to{\mathbb R}, \qquad \zeta_{r,k}(y)=\inf\{\zeta_r(F^ky'):s(y,y')\ge 2k\},
\]
for $r=1,2$ and $k\ge1$.
Then $\zeta_{r,k}={\bar{\zeta}}_{r,k}\circ {\bar{\pi}}$ where
${\bar{\zeta}}_{r,k}\in L^\infty({\bar Y})$ with
$|{\bar{\zeta}}_{r,k}|_\infty\le |\zeta_r|_\infty$. It is standard that
$|\zeta_r\circ F^k-\zeta_{r,k}|_\infty\ll \gamma^k$. Moreover, we can choose $\gamma$ so that
$\sup_k\|R^k{\bar{\zeta}}_{r,k}\|<\infty$.

Let ${\tilde u}_n={\bar u}_n\circ{\bar{\pi}}$. Since $v$ is locally constant, there exists ${\bar v}^{(n)}$ such that
${\hat v}^{(n)}={\bar v}^{(n)}\circ{\bar{\pi}}$. Then 
\begin{align*}
\int_Y & \zeta_1\;\zeta_2\circ F^n \;1_{\{{\tilde u}_n\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\hat v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\,d\mu
\\ & =
\int_Y \zeta_1\circ F^k\;\zeta_2\circ F^{n+k} \,1_{\{{\tilde u}_n\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\hat v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\circ F^k\,d\mu
 = J_1+J_2+J_3,
\end{align*}
where
\begin{align*}
J_1 & = 
\int_Y (\zeta_1\circ F^k-\zeta_{1,k})\;\zeta_2\circ F^{n+k} 
\,1_{\{{\tilde u}_n\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\hat v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\circ F^k\,d\mu
\ll \gamma^k, \\
J_2 & = 
\int_Y \zeta_{1,k}\;(\zeta_2\circ F^k-\zeta_{2,k})\circ F^n 
\,1_{\{{\tilde u}_n\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\hat v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\circ F^k\,d\mu
\ll \gamma^k, \\
J_3 & = 
\int_Y \zeta_{1,k}\;\zeta_{2,k}\circ F^n 
\,1_{\{{\tilde u}_n\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\hat v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\circ F^k\,d\mu
 \\ & =
\int_{\bar Y} {\bar{\zeta}}_{1,k}\;{\bar{\zeta}}_{2,k}\circ {\bar F}^n 
\,1_{\{{\bar u}_n\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\bar v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\circ {\bar F}^k\,d{\bar{\mu}}
 \\ & =
\int_{\bar Y} \big(R^k{\bar{\zeta}}_{1,k}\big)\;{\bar{\zeta}}_{2,k}\circ {\bar F}^{n-k} 
\,1_{\{{\bar u}_n\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\bar v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\,d{\bar{\mu}}.
\end{align*}
We take $k=q\log n$ where $q$ is sufficiently large that $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n^m\gamma^{q\log n}=0$.
Then
\[
a_n^m\int_Y \zeta_1\;\zeta_2\circ F^n \;1_{\{{\tilde u}_n\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\hat v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\,d\mu
= \nu_{n,z}(K)+o(1)
\]
as $n\to\infty$ uniformly in $z$, where
\[
\nu_{n,z}(K)=a_n^m\int_{\bar Y} \big(R^k{\bar{\zeta}}_{1,k}\big)\;{\bar{\zeta}}_{2,k}\circ {\bar F}^{n-k} 
\,1_{\{{\bar u}_n\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\bar v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\,d{\bar{\mu}}.
\]

Let $D={\mathbb R}^{m_1}\times[-\pi,\pi]^{m_2}\times{\bar Y}$ and $q=n-k$.
Proceeding as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:LLT},
\begin{align*}
(2\pi)^{m_2} & \int_{{\mathbb R}^{m_1}}h \,d\nu_{n,w}  \\ & =
                                  
                                   
                                                                        
                                    
          
a_n^m\int_De^{-is_1\cdot w_1a_n}
e^{-is_2\cdot([w_2a_n]+c_n)}\hat h(s_1)
\big(R^k{\bar{\zeta}}_{1,k}\big)\;{\bar{\zeta}}_{2,k}\circ {\bar F}^q e^{is\cdot {\overline{\Psi}}_n}
\,d{\bar{\mu}}\,ds
 \\ &  =
a_n^m\int_{D}e^{-is_1\cdot w_1a_n}e^{-is_2\cdot([w_2a_n]+c_n)}\hat h(s_1)
\big(R^k{\bar{\zeta}}_{1,k}\big)\;\big({\bar{\zeta}}_{2,k}e^{is\cdot{\overline{\Psi}}_k}\big)\circ {\bar F}^q e^{is\cdot {\overline{\Psi}}_q}\,
d{\bar{\mu}}\,ds,
\end{align*}
where ${\bar{\Psi}}=\big({\bar u},v-\int_Y v\,d\mu\big)$
and $c_n=\big[n\int_Y v\,d\mu\big]-n\int_Y v\,d\mu$.
Hence, by Lemma~\ref{lem:LLT},
\begin{align*}
\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}h\,d\nu_{n,w} & =
 I_1 + O(\|R^k{\bar{\zeta}}_{1,k} \|\,{\textstyle\sup_s}|{\bar{\zeta}}_{2,k}e^{is\cdot{\overline{\Psi}}_k}  |_1 a_n^m a_q^{-(m+1)})=I_1+O(a_n^{-1})
\end{align*}
where
\begin{align*}
I_1  
 & = a_n^m {\bar{\mu}}\big(R^k{\bar{\zeta}}_{1,k}\big)\,
\int_{|s|< {\epsilon} }
e^{-is_1\cdot w_1a_n}e^{-is_2\cdot([w_2a_n]+c_n)}\hat h(s) 
{\bar{\mu}}\big({\bar{\zeta}}_{2,k}e^{is\cdot{\overline{\Psi}}_k}\big)\,
\lambda(s)^q ds
 \\ & = {\bar{\mu}}\big(R^k{\bar{\zeta}}_{1,k}\big)\,
\int_{|s|< a_n {\epsilon} }
e^{-is_1\cdot w_1}e^{-ia_n^{-1}s_2\cdot([w_2a_n]+c_n)}\hat h(a_n^{-1}s) 
{\bar{\mu}}\big({\bar{\zeta}}_{2,k}e^{ia_n^{-1}s\cdot{\overline{\Psi}}_k}\big)\,
\lambda(a_n^{-1}s)^q ds.
\end{align*}
But
\begin{align*}
{\bar{\mu}}\big(R^k{\bar{\zeta}}_{1,k}\big) & =
\mu\big( \zeta_{1,k}\big)=\mu\big( \zeta_1\big)+O(\gamma^k), \\
{\bar{\mu}}\big( {\bar{\zeta}}_{2,k}e^{is\cdot{\overline{\Psi}}_k}\big) & =
\mu\big( \zeta_{2,k}e^{is\cdot{\widetilde \Psi}_k}\big)=
\mu\big( \zeta_2\circ F^k e^{is\cdot{\widetilde \Psi}_k}\big)+O(\gamma^k).
\end{align*}
Hence
\begin{align*}
\lim_{n\to\infty,\,w\to z}
\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}h\,d\nu_{n,w}  & =
\mu(\zeta_1)\,\mu(\zeta_2)\,
\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}\hat h(0)e^{-s\cdot x}{\mathbb E}(e^{is\cdot X_\alpha})\,ds
\\ & =
\mu(\zeta_1)\,\mu(\zeta_2)\,
\int_{{\mathbb R}^m}h(x)\,dx\,g_{X_\alpha}(z).
\end{align*}
As in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:LLT}, it follows from~\cite[Theorem~10.7]{Breiman} that
 \[
\lim_{n\to\infty} \sup_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{z\in{\mathbb R}^m}{|z|\le L}}
\Big|a_n^m\int_Y \zeta_1\;\zeta_2\circ F^n \; 
1_{\{{\tilde u}_n\in z_1a_n+K,\,{\hat v}^{(n)}=[z_2a_n]\}}\,d\mu
- g_{X_\alpha}(z)\mu(\zeta_1)\mu(\zeta_2) |K|\Big|=0.
\]

Next, given a measurable subset $A\subset{\mathcal A}$ with
$\mu(\partial A)= 0$, we approximate $A$ and $Y\setminus A$ from within as in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:A}. In place of cylinders $\beta_n$, we use sets of the form $\beta_n(y)=\{F^ny':s(y,y')>2n\}$. Similarly for $B$. In this way, we obtain that
\begin{align*}
\lim_{n\to\infty} \sup_{\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{z\in{\mathbb R}^m}{|z|\le L}}
\Big|a_n^m\mu\big(y\in A\cap  F^{-n}B:\, {\tilde u}_n(y) & \in z_1a_n +K,
\, {\hat v}^{(n)}(y)=[z_2a_n]   \big)
\\ & - g_{X_\alpha}(z)\mu(A)\mu(B)|K|\Big|=0
\end{align*}
for $A,B,K$ as in the statement of the Theorem.


Finally, we use the same argument as in Subsection~\ref{sec:pf2} to pass from
${\tilde u}_n$ to
$u_n={\tilde u}_n+\chi\circ F^n-\chi$.
By assumption, $\chi$ restricts to a uniformly continuous function on $A$ and $B$. Hence
a simpler version of the argument in Proposition~\ref{prop:N4} shows that
the functions $H_1=-\chi$ and $H_2=\chi$
satisfy condition~\ref{itm:H}.
We can now apply Lemma~\ref{lem:vague} to deduce the result.
